brief.headline: Aluminium fell for a second session but the shape of the curve turned bullish underneath it: the official cash settlement lost $28.50 (-0.86%) on 13-August while the front of the curve flipped out of contango into a $4.00 backwardation, so the price of metal fell at the same time as the premium for having it immediately rose. The move was driven by two public, forward-dated supply headlines - a war-damaged Gulf smelter guiding a return to pre-incident output in the first quarter of 2027, and a government support package securing Australia's largest smelter with power contracted to 2038 - neither of which adds a tonne to the prompt market this week.
bullets: WHAT MOVED. LME official cash aluminium settled $3,279.00 on 13-August, down $28.50 (-0.86%) from $3,307.50, and the three-month settled $3,275.00, down $33.50 (-1.01%). That is a second consecutive fall but at less than half the pace of the previous session. Measured from the 11-August high of $3,373.00 the two-day give-back is $94.00 (-2.79%); measured from the 28-July swing low the market is still up $119.50 (+3.78%), so roughly three fifths of the August advance is intact. Every metal on the base complex fell on the same session - zinc -1.39%, aluminium -1.01%, lead -0.94%, copper -0.84%, nickel -0.53% - which points at a shared macro or positioning factor rather than anything specific to aluminium.

WHY THE CURVE MATTERS MORE THAN THE PRICE TODAY. The three-month fell $5.00 more than cash did, and that asymmetry flipped the cash-to-three-month spread out of a $1.00 contango into a $4.00 backwardation - the first prompt premium since 10-August. Backwardation means buyers are paying more for metal today than for metal in three months, which is the market's own signal that prompt availability is tight. Spread and flat price therefore moved in OPPOSITE directions, and for the first time in this sequence the divergence points the constructive way. Keep it in proportion: $4.00 is 0.12% of the price - a marginal prompt premium, not a squeeze - and the front end has still not held a premium two sessions running since 04-August.

WHY THE SELLING HAPPENED, AND WHY IT IS ABOUT 2027 RATHER THAN THIS WEEK. Two public headlines did the work. A major Gulf producer's half-year earnings release, published 12-August, disclosed that its war-damaged smelter is running at about 18% of capacity and guided hot-metal production back to pre-incident levels in the first quarter of 2027, with roughly US$400 million of capital allocated to the recovery. Then on 13-August the owners of Australia's largest aluminium smelter secured a A$2.5 billion government support package, a ten-year power purchase agreement running to 2038 and a A$1.1 billion investment commitment, removing a closure risk that had hung over roughly 590,000 tonnes a year of capacity. Both improve the supply picture for 2027 and beyond. Neither changes the number of tonnes available next week, which is exactly why the forward tenors sold off harder than the prompt date.

WHAT TO WATCH NEXT. First, whether the backwardation survives a third session - a prompt premium that persists while flat price falls would be the first genuine evidence in this cycle that the physical market is tightening independently of financial positioning, and the reverse would mark today as noise. Second, the exchange stock line: warehouse inventories fell another 1,700 tonnes to 250,000 tonnes, a 32nd consecutive daily draw and a fresh cycle low, and a 33rd draw on a third down day would sharpen the divergence further. Third, whether the alumina side finally prints: a 6.3 Mt/y refinery has been running at half rate since 11-August on a gas supply disruption and no public seaborne alumina transaction dated after that disclosure has yet appeared to size the cost impact.

kpis.label: LME 3-Month
kpis.note: 13-Aug 3-MONTH OFFICIAL $3,275.00 against $3,308.50 = -$33.50 (-1.01%), a LARGER fall than cash took. THE ASYMMETRY IS THE POINT AND IT IS THE EXACT OPPOSITE OF YESTERDAY. On 12-August both legs fell by an identical $65.50 in a perfectly parallel shift; today the forward leg fell $5.00 more than the prompt leg, which is how a curve flips from contango into backwardation. Selling concentrated in the forward tenors while the prompt date held relatively better is the signature of a market repricing a FUTURE supply expectation - and the two public headlines behind the move, EGA's Q1-2027 recovery date and the Tomago power settlement running to 2038, are both about supply in 2027 and beyond rather than supply this month. The 1.618x extension objective at $3,392 was never reached; the high stands at $3,374.00 from 11-August. SECONDARY, DIFFERENT-BASIS REFERENCE FOR THE SAME DAY, QUOTED ONLY AS CORROBORATION AND NOT MIXED INTO THIS ROW: Trading Economics' independent CFD series marks $3,241.50 for 13-August, down 1.97% on a prior mark of $3,306.75, still +2.08% on the month and +23.52% year-on-year, and its news stream attributes the fall directly to EGA's Al Taweelah timeline and the Australian smelter support package. An independent series agreeing on direction, on rough magnitude and on CAUSE is the strongest form of corroboration available on a public board. avg = the JULY-2026 3-month official monthly mean of $3,149.50 computed across the same 23 published July sessions.

kpis.label: Cash-3M spread
kpis.note: FLIPPED INTO A $4.00 BACKWARDATION FROM A $1.00 CONTANGO - THE FIRST BACKWARDATION SINCE 10-AUGUST AND THE SINGLE MOST INFORMATIVE NUMBER ON THIS PAGE TODAY. Cash $3,279.00 now sits $4.00 ABOVE 3-month $3,275.00. CONVENTION, STATED EXPLICITLY: cash above 3M is BACKWARDATION and signals prompt tightness; cash below 3M is CONTANGO and signals prompt comfort. SPREAD AND FLAT PRICE MOVED IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS AND THE DIVERGENCE IS NOW POINTING THE BULLISH WAY FOR THE FIRST TIME IN THIS SEQUENCE. All week the complaint on this page was that flat price kept making new highs while the front end surrendered its premium - buying that was forward-dated rather than prompt. Today the mirror image arrived: flat price fell for a second session and the front end RECLAIMED a premium. Read together, the two configurations say the same thing from opposite ends - the marginal price-setter in this market is positioned in the forward tenors, not at the prompt date. THE AUGUST SEQUENCE NOW READS: +$48.00, +$34.50, a $0.50 contango, +$1.00, a $0.50 contango, +$7.00, a $1.00 contango, a $1.00 contango, and now +$4.00 - six of ten August sessions in backwardation, and the front end has still not held a premium for two consecutive sessions since 04-August, which is the caveat that keeps this from being a trend. PROPORTION, BECAUSE IT MATTERS: $4.00 is 0.12% of cash. This is a marginal prompt premium, not a squeeze. The correct words are 'the front end firmed', not 'the market is tight'. avg = the July-2026 mean cash-3M spread of +$6.48 across the 23 published July sessions, so today sits $2.48 BELOW the July norm - much closer to it than at any point this week.

lme.commentary: A SECOND DOWN SESSION AT HALF THE PACE OF THE FIRST, AND A CURVE THAT TURNED THE OTHER WAY UNDERNEATH IT. The 13-August official put cash at $3,279.00 (-$28.50, -0.86%) and the 3-month at $3,275.00 (-$33.50, -1.01%). Because the forward leg fell $5.00 more than the prompt leg, the cash-3M spread flipped out of a $1.00 contango into a $4.00 BACKWARDATION - the first prompt premium since 10-August. SPREAD AND FLAT PRICE MOVED IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS, which the convention on this board requires be called out explicitly: cash above 3M is backwardation and signals prompt tightness; cash below 3M is contango and signals prompt comfort. Yesterday's fall was a perfectly parallel shift with the spread pinned flat; today's was concentrated in the forward tenors. That is the signature of a market repricing a FUTURE supply expectation rather than a present one, and the two headlines behind the move fit exactly - a Gulf smelter's recovery guided to Q1-2027 and an Australian smelter's power contracted to 2038. Exchange stock fell another 1,700 t to 250,000 t, a 32nd consecutive draw and a fresh cycle low, so for a second day the metal actually available on warrant shrank while the price fell. Keep the whole thing in proportion: $4.00 is 0.12% of cash, the two-day give-back of $94.00 is roughly two fifths of the August advance, and the market remains $119.50 (+3.78%) above the 28-July swing low.

THE Q4 ARGUMENT MOVED TODAY, AND IT MOVED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS AT ONCE. For sellers: the LME front end flipped into a $4.00 backwardation and exchange stock drew for a 32nd consecutive session to a fresh cycle low, so the prompt-tightness case is marginally STRONGER than it was yesterday. For buyers: a major Gulf producer published a dated recovery path on 12-August guiding its war-damaged smelter back to pre-incident hot metal in Q1-2027, and Australia's largest smelter was secured by a government support package on 13-August - two public facts that make the 2027 regional supply picture visibly better and give buyers a forward argument they did not have a week ago. Neither is a premium assessment and neither is being treated as one here.

Those two facts pull European smelter economics in opposite directions - more local metal, dearer feedstock - and neither has yet shown up in a public premium assessment.

Reading the US premium as a signal of American physical scarcity without stripping the tariff leg out first is the most common error on this datapoint.

drivers.text: The front end flipped into backwardation on a down day - the prompt-tightness case got marginally stronger, not weaker — Cash settled $3,279.00 against a 3-month of $3,275.00, a $4.00 BACKWARDATION, reversing a $1.00 contango. Because the 3-month fell $33.50 while cash fell only $28.50, the selling was concentrated in the forward tenors and the prompt date held relatively better. For a premium negotiation this is the cleanest available public evidence that prompt metal is not in surplus, and it arrived on a session when the flat price fell - which is when a purely financial explanation would predict the opposite. Proportion matters: $4.00 is 0.12% of cash, a marginal premium rather than a squeeze.

A 32nd consecutive stock draw took warehouse inventory to a fresh cycle low on the second down day running — LME aluminium stock fell another 1,700 t to 250,000 t on 13-August, a 32nd uninterrupted daily draw and the lowest of the cycle. Six weeks of continuous draws is the single strongest public argument for physical tightness available on this board, and it continued through a two-session, $94.00 price decline - which is precisely when a purely financially-motivated draw would be expected to pause. Copper drew 4,400 t to 207,725 t on the same session while its backwardation widened from $175.00 to $203.00.
drivers.source: Westmetall - LME aluminium and copper stock series, 13-Aug-2026 session

drivers.text: The first genuinely new supply-RELIEF facts of the cycle published in the last 48 hours, and they cap the ceiling — Emirates Global Aluminium's H1-2026 earnings release on 12-August disclosed that the war-damaged Al Taweelah smelter is running at about 18% of capacity and guided hot metal back to pre-incident levels in Q1-2027, with roughly US$400 million of capital allocated to the recovery programme. On 13-August the owners of Tomago, Australia's largest smelter at up to 590,000 t/y, secured a A$2.5 billion federal and state support package, a ten-year power purchase agreement running to 2038 and an A$1.1 billion investment commitment. Both are dated, sourced and forward-looking; neither adds prompt tonnes. Premium buyers negotiating a Q4 number now have a supply-relief argument they did not have a week ago.
drivers.source: Mining.com.au - Aluminium falls as war-hit smelter eyes faster restart (14-Aug-2026)

drivers.text: Chinese physical buyers stayed on the sidelines into the weekend and downstream alloy quotes were cut again — SMM's 14-August South China review reports futures extending sharp losses with spot in the doldrums, holders lowering offers into discounts of -10 to 0 yuan/mt as bearish sentiment built ahead of the weekend, and downstream buyers initially standing aside on expectations of lower prices before restocking only in limited volume. Transactions concentrated at premiums of 60-100 yuan/mt over the SHFE 2608 contract. Separately, ADC12 secondary alloy quotes were cut a further 200 yuan/mt on falling metal and scrap costs. Physical buyers resisting at the margin caps the demand-pull component of any premium.
drivers.source: SMM - Futures Continue to Plunge, Spot Aluminum Adjusts in the Doldrums (14-Aug-2026)

prices.label: Alumina FOB East Australia (SMM reported trade)
prices.note: HELD AT $356/mt FOB EAST AUSTRALIA (SMM-reported transaction of 30,000 mt for September loading dealt 05-Aug-2026, published 06-Aug). NO PUBLIC SEABORNE ALUMINA PRICE PRINT DATED AFTER THE ALUNORTE DISCLOSURE HAS BEEN FOUND AT THIS COMPILE, SO NO VALUE ON THIS PANEL IS CHANGED FOR A THIRD RUN - the event is recorded, the price is not invented. The next public transaction print is the datapoint that converts the Alunorte headline into a cost fact, and three days on it has still not arrived. THE SUPPLY EVENT, RESTATED BECAUSE IT IS STILL THE DOMINANT ALUMINA FACT AND IS NOW IN ITS THIRD DAY: Norsk Hydro disclosed on 11-August that Alunorte in Barcarena, Para - 6.3 Mt/y nameplate and the largest alumina refinery outside China - reduced production to 50 percent after gas supplier CELBA notified disruptions to natural gas availability, and guides a potential Q3-2026 Bauxite & Alumina impact of US$75-100 million while calling the full impact uncertain. Contingency measures announced were spot gas purchases and a request for direct access to the Barcarena LNG regasification terminal. Roughly 3 Mt/y of annualised alumina is off the seaborne balance for an unspecified period and NO follow-up disclosure has published in three days. THE OTHER RECENT PRINT, STATED SEPARATELY BECAUSE THE BASIS DIFFERS AND MUST NOT BE BLENDED: SMM published on 11-August that 30,000 mt traded at $365/mt CIF MALAYSIA for September shipment, dealt 07-Aug-2026. CIF Malaysia is a delivered price including freight; FOB East Australia is a load-port price, so the $9/mt gap is broadly freight rather than a $9/mt rally. The honest read on the two together is that the seaborne market held around the mid-$350s FOB through the first week of August. MARGIN CONTEXT AT TODAY'S LOWER METAL PRICE, AND THE RATIO MOVED AGAINST SMELTERS FOR A SECOND SESSION: against the 13-August three-month official of $3,275.00 the FOB mark now sits at about 10.9% of the metal price and the CIF mark at about 11.1%, up from 10.8% and 11.0% yesterday purely because metal fell again. Both remain well below the decade rule of thumb of roughly 15-17%, so the alumina leg is still a TAILWIND to smelter economics - but the tailwind narrows mechanically every time metal falls, and Alunorte remains the first credible threat to it this year.

prices.note: Platts FOB Australia - NO PUBLIC MARK AT AN AUGUST 2026 DATE. The Platts alumina index and the Fastmarkets MB-ALU-0002 index are subscription products and are not publicly quotable. The last independently verifiable public Platts level is $304/mt on 15-Apr-2026, with Q1-2026 averaging $306.91/mt (-2.82% quarter-on-quarter); the $330/t carried here derives from a 26-Jun reference in S&P Global coverage. The value and date are CARRIED UNCHANGED and are explicitly stale - the two SMM-reported transactions above ($356/mt FOB East Australia dealt 05-Aug, $365/mt CIF Malaysia dealt 07-Aug) are far fresher and should be read as the live market. Both sit well above this carried index level, so the direction of travel since late June has been UP, and the Alunorte cut points the same way. A USEFUL INDEPENDENT CROSS-CHECK REMAINS South32's FY26 operating report, which gives average REALISED alumina prices of $363/t at Worsley (down 30% year-on-year from $518/t) and $356/t at Brazil Alumina (down 36% from $555/t) across the full financial year to June 2026. Those are annual realisations on a different basis from a spot index and must not be blended into this row, but they independently place the market in the mid-$350s to low-$360s and confirm how far alumina has fallen year-on-year.

prices.label: SMM Alumina Index (China)
prices.note: SMM Alumina Index (China domestic). Carried at its stated date - no fresher public print was returned this run. THE MOST USEFUL RECENT CHINESE ALUMINA DATAPOINT REMAINS A COST NUMBER, NOT A PRICE: SMM published on 11-August that China's national weighted-average FULL production cost for alumina was RMB 2,718/mt in July, UP RMB 37/mt month-on-month, with the weighted-average CASH cost at RMB 2,544/mt. SMM guides August full cost to RMB 2,700-2,820/mt and cash cost to RMB 2,530-2,650/mt. The rise is attributed almost entirely to bauxite - higher imported CIF costs on elevated ocean freight plus the Guinea rainy season, and persistently tight domestic ore after mining-accident after-effects slowed restarts - partly offset by a small decline in energy costs. NOTE THE ASYMMETRY THIS CREATES WITH THE ALUNORTE EVENT: China's alumina cost floor is rising for domestic reasons at the same time as roughly 3 Mt/y of non-Chinese seaborne supply sits at half rate. The two are independent and they push the same way.

prices.label: Bauxite (SMM imported index / Guinea CIF China)
prices.note: Carried at the 06-Aug-2026 SMM Bauxite Weekly Review. THE NEXT EDITION IS DUE TODAY on the publication's Thursday cadence and had not printed at this 03:40 London compile, so the row is carried rather than marked. SMM Imported Bauxite Index $71.57/mt, UP $0.70 week-on-week, Guinea CIF $70-74/mt (average +$1 w/w), Guinea FOB $38-42/mt (average +$1 w/w). CORROBORATION FROM THE 11-AUGUST COST REVIEW: imported bauxite prices 'sustained their upward trend in July, serving as the core driver behind the cost surge', citing elevated ocean freight and the Guinea rainy season reducing shipments, plus slow domestic Chinese mine resumption - to the point that 'some alumina producers have been forced to adjust production schedules'. SMM's forward view: 'no clear timeline has emerged for domestic supply recovery, while imported ore shipments are expected to shrink further amid the rainy season. Bauxite prices are likely to hold high and steady, with import quotes potentially edging slightly higher.' STRUCTURAL DEVELOPMENT CARRIED FROM LAST RUN: Guinea's Mines Minister Bouna Sylla said state-owned Nimba Mining will sell bauxite to global traders and miners through MONTHLY TENDERS, with minimum guaranteed annual volumes under partner agreements and additional output sold via monthly spot tenders; CEO Patrice L'Huillier named Mercuria, Glencore, Rio Tinto and Vedanta as potential partners. Monthly tendering adds genuine public price discovery to the world's most important seaborne bauxite source and simultaneously shifts volume from contract to spot, which raises price variance in an already tight rainy-season market. THE NEXT SCHEDULED HARD DATAPOINT REMAINS THE GUINEA AUGUST LONG-TERM CONTRACT, still under negotiation against July's settlement of $70-71.5/mt. DRIVER DOWN, UNCHANGED: Chinese refinery bauxite inventories at roughly 94 days of cover. This remains the best-evidenced upward-trending input on the whole board.

prices.label: Caustic soda (China alumina-plant contract, Shanxi)
prices.note: CNY 2,090/t delivered, 50% ion-membrane liquid on a 100% NaOH basis - the JULY purchase price at Shanxi alumina plants, held flat month-on-month. THE VALUE IS DELIBERATELY NOT CHANGED because August contracts have not settled and no new public mark was returned this run. GUIDANCE CARRIED AND IT IS WHY THE TREND FLAG IS UP: SMM's alumina cost review states that Shanxi caustic soda long-term contract prices are EXPECTED TO RISE BY RMB 50/mt in August, while Guangxi prices are set to DECLINE FURTHER BY RMB 150/mt. That is an explicit regional divergence, not a national move: the north tightens slightly, the south loosens and widens its cost advantage. SMM's assessment of the aggregate effect is that caustic 'had limited impact on alumina production costs' in July and will show 'overall narrow fluctuations' in August. AN EXPECTATION IS NOT A SETTLEMENT: the RMB 50/mt is carried as guidance in this note only and has not been written into the value, which stays at the last settled July figure.

Against the 13-August three-month official of $3,275.00 the FOB East Australia mark of $356/mt is about 10.9% of the metal price, against 10.8% yesterday and 10.6% the day before. The alumina leg remains a clear TAILWIND to smelter economics at roughly two thirds of the decade-normal 15-17% ratio, but the arithmetic works both ways: every dollar off the metal price narrows the tailwind without alumina doing anything at all.

THE TWO SIDES OF THE FEEDSTOCK ARGUMENT ARE NOW BOTH VISIBLE AND THEY ARE INDEPENDENT. Outside China, roughly 3 Mt/y of annualised seaborne alumina is at half rate on a gas availability problem that is harder to fix quickly than a commercial dispute. Inside China, the national weighted-average full production cost rose RMB 37/mt month-on-month in July on bauxite, with SMM guiding August higher again. Neither depends on the other and both push the alumina cost floor up. What is missing is a price print to confirm the market agrees.

items.label: Calcined petroleum coke (CPC, anode-grade)
items.note: Calcined petroleum coke, the largest single carbon input to a prebaked anode. THE CHARTED SERIES IS THE FEEDSTOCK, NOT THE CALCINED PRODUCT: hist tracks China green petroleum coke 3B settlement and quarterly average marks in RMB/t, which is the publicly-settled series with a consistent basis; the headline value is the indicative international CPC range in $/t. The two are stated separately and must not be blended. NO NEW PUBLIC MARK THIS RUN - the monthly settlement window falls around the 17th-18th, so the next opportunity to append a sourced pair is three to four days away. The risk into that window is to the upside: Brent has spent August well above the pre-crisis reference and green coke is a refinery by-product, so crude strength feeds the calcining chain with a lag.

items.label: Coal tar pitch (CTP)
items.note: Coal tar pitch, the binder in a prebaked anode, on the Chinese monthly settlement cycle in RMB/t as published via SMM and AL Circle. NO NEW PUBLIC MARK THIS RUN. The settlement window falls around the 17th-18th of each month and the last appended pair is the June-2026 cycle at RMB 4,940/t, up from RMB 4,726/t in May. A two-point series is the correct shape for a monthly settlement - gaps are left as gaps rather than interpolated.

items.label: Pre-baked anodes
items.note: Prebaked anodes, Chinese monthly settlement basis in RMB/t via SMM and AL Circle. NO NEW PUBLIC MARK THIS RUN - the July-2026 cycle at RMB 5,683/t remains the latest appended pair and the August cycle settles around the 17th-18th. Anodes are the largest non-alumina, non-power cost line in a smelter and the settlement carries the pass-through from both calcined coke and coal tar pitch, so the mid-month window is the highest-value scheduled data event on this basket.

items.label: Electricity (smelter power)
items.note: Smelter power. NO PUBLIC PRICE SERIES EXISTS FOR THIS ROW AND hist IS DELIBERATELY EMPTY - smelter power is overwhelmingly contracted bilaterally or through long-dated PPAs and captive generation, and those terms are not public, so any 'series' here would be fabricated. The indicative $30-60/MWh range spans the global cost curve rather than describing any particular asset. THE MOST IMPORTANT PUBLIC POWER FACT IN MONTHS PUBLISHED ON 13-AUGUST: the owners of Tomago, Australia's largest smelter at up to 590,000 t/y and New South Wales' largest single electricity user, secured a A$2.5 billion federal and state support package and a ten-year power purchase agreement running to 2038, fully renewable from 2033, alongside an A$1.1 billion investment commitment including A$100 million for decarbonisation. It demonstrates the live economics of the power line: a smelter of that scale required public support to contract power at all, and the deal is explicitly conditioned on demand-response obligations during grid stress. European TTF gas, the marginal power input for the EU smelter fleet, marks EUR 60.21/MWh on the Trading Economics board, down 0.32% on the day.

items.label: Aluminium fluoride (AlF3)
items.note: Aluminium fluoride (AlF3), Chinese market range in RMB/t on the SMM fluoride-salts weekly cycle. NO NEW PUBLIC MARK APPENDED THIS RUN. THE RULE ON THIS BOARD IS THAT AN UNDATED QUOTE IS NOT A MARK: rather than append a pair that cannot be dated, the gap is left open and the last dated pairs stand. items.label: Cryolite / bath makeup
items.note: Cryolite / bath makeup, Chinese market range in RMB/t on the SMM fluoride-salts weekly cycle. NO NEW PUBLIC MARK APPENDED THIS RUN, for the same reason as the aluminium fluoride row above - the fluoride commentary returned this run could not be tied to a verifiable August-2026 date, and an undated quote is not a mark. Cryolite is a small line by value but a hard constraint operationally, because bath chemistry cannot be deferred the way a capital project can.

items.label: Cathode / graphite blocks
items.note: Cathode / graphite blocks. NO PUBLIC PRICE SERIES EXISTS FOR THIS ROW AND hist IS DELIBERATELY EMPTY - cathode blocks are bought on multi-year contracts against qualification-specific specifications and there is no publicly quoted index, so a series here would be invented. items.note: Silicon metal, Chinese market ranges in RMB/t via SMM. NO NEW PUBLIC MARK APPENDED THIS RUN - the 06-August pair at RMB 9,050/t remains the latest. items.note: Magnesium (99.9%), Chinese Fugu/Shenmu market range in RMB/t plus the FOB Tianjin export reference in $/t, via SMM. items.note: LME copper official CASH settlement, 13-Aug-2026 board, cross-checked on the English and German Westmetall overviews. items.note: Ti-B grain refiner (AlTi5B1). NO PUBLIC PRICE SERIES EXISTS FOR THIS ROW AND hist IS DELIBERATELY EMPTY - grain refiner is a contracted specialty consumable with no publicly quoted index. logistics.label: Strait of Hormuz transit
logistics.note: EFFECTIVELY CLOSED TO COMMERCIAL SHIPPING, DAY 166 SINCE THE 28-FEBRUARY SHUTDOWN, AND UNCHANGED IN SUBSTANCE THIS RUN. No public development has been reported since Iran's state broadcaster restated on 11-August that the Strait remains closed until conditions are met. Trading Economics' 14-August cross-asset stream carries both Brent and WTI headlines framed as 'Holds Decline Amid Hormuz Stalemate', which is the market's own word for it - a stalemate, not a resolution and not an escalation. THIS IS SIMULTANEOUSLY THE LARGEST STRUCTURAL SUPPORT UNDER THE ALUMINIUM PRICE AND THE LARGEST SINGLE-HEADLINE DOWNSIDE RISK. The Gulf was around a tenth of global primary production before the conflict. Note the interaction with today's move, because it is the sharpest thing on this panel: the market has just repriced ONE Gulf supply variable - a single smelter's recovery date - and took nearly 3% out of the price in two sessions. A change in the Hormuz regime itself would be an order of magnitude larger.

logistics.label: Red Sea / Bab al Mandeb corridor
logistics.note: Unchanged in substance and it should not be conflated with Hormuz. Most operators continue to route around the Cape of Good Hope, which adds roughly 10-14 days and the associated bunker and charter cost to Asia-Europe voyages. The 09-August strike on the Jazan refinery is a Red Sea littoral event rather than a Strait closure, and its relevance here is that it keeps war-risk pricing elevated across the whole basin rather than that it blocks any particular lane.

logistics.label: Gulf war-risk insurance
logistics.note: War-risk cover for a VLCC transit is estimated at roughly 30 times pre-crisis levels on published market commentary. The mechanism that matters for a metals board is generic: war-risk premium is a per-voyage cost that lands on delivered prices regardless of who is shipping, so it inflates every regional premium that involves a Gulf leg without telling you anything about metal availability. It is a freight cost wearing a premium's clothing.

logistics.label: Baltic Dry Index (BDI)
logistics.note: Carried at its stated date of 07-August - no fresher public print was returned this run and the value is explicitly stale rather than re-stated as current. The last public reading was the sixth consecutive gain. Dry bulk freight matters to this board mainly through bauxite and alumina: SMM identified elevated ocean freight on imported bauxite as one of the two drivers of the RMB 37/mt month-on-month rise in China's alumina production cost in July, alongside the Guinea rainy season. A rising BDI is therefore a slow upward push on the alumina cost floor, felt with a lag of weeks rather than days.

logistics.label: Container freight (Drewry WCI)
logistics.note: Carried at its stated date and explicitly stale. Container rates matter far less to primary metal than dry bulk does - ingot and billet move in bulk or breakbulk - but they are the best public proxy for the Cape-of-Good-Hope reroute surcharge that sits on Asia-Europe value-added and downstream flows.

logistics.label: Incoterms / demurrage
logistics.note: Unchanged in mechanics and the point is generic rather than specific to any counterparty. With Hormuz closed for a 166th day and war-risk cover roughly 30 times pre-crisis, force-majeure and war-risk clauses are the operative commercial terms across the region, and demurrage exposure rises with every day of routing uncertainty. Nothing on this row is a company position - it is a description of how contracts in the region are behaving as publicly reported.

row.label: Brent crude
row.note: Brent marks $86.778 on the Trading Economics cross-asset board at this 14-August compile, down 0.34% and down from $88.039 at yesterday's compile - a second soft session with the headline framed as 'Brent Holds Decline Amid Hormuz Stalemate'. Downward: a softening crude price is the market marking down its own estimate of Gulf supply risk, which is the same thing aluminium did on the EGA headline. When crude and aluminium fall together on a Gulf-risk repricing, the anode-cost channel is the one that lags.

row.note: European gas marks EUR 60.21/MWh, down 0.32% and effectively flat against yesterday's EUR 60.13. TTF is the marginal power input for the European smelter fleet and therefore the cleanest public proxy for the EU cost curve. A flat gas price alongside a falling metal price is a margin compression for European smelters, and it is the backdrop against which the Slovalco restart of about +75,000 t/y remains funded for Q4-2026.

Commodity weakness on a strengthening dollar is a currency story; commodity weakness on a flat dollar is a supply-and-positioning story, which is what the two public headlines behind this session describe.

row.label: EUR/USD
row.note: Trading Economics marks 1.15362 at this compile. The LME's own 13-August fixings printed EUR/USD MTLE 1.15350, the ECB fixing 1.15340 and BFIX 1.15337, all three rolling together onto the 13-August session - which is one of the internal-consistency checks used to confirm the whole board belongs to a single ring rather than a cached snapshot. headlines.title: A SECOND DOWN SESSION, BUT AT HALF THE PACE. The 13-August LME official put cash at $3,279.00, down $28.50 (-0.86%), and the 3-month at $3,275.00, down $33.50 (-1.01%). Cumulative give-back from the 11-August high of $3,373.00 is $94.00 (-2.79%), which is roughly two fifths of the August advance. The market is still $119.50 (+3.78%) above the 28-July swing low of $3,159.50 and $83.00 (+2.60%) above the 31-July official, so three fifths of the move survives. THE DECELERATION MATTERS: a $65.50 fall followed by a $28.50 fall is a market finding a level, not a market breaking.

THE FRONT END RECLAIMED A PREMIUM ON A DOWN DAY - THE MOST INFORMATIVE THING ON THE BOARD TODAY. The 3-month fell $33.50 while cash fell $28.50, so the cash-3M spread flipped out of a $1.00 contango into a $4.00 BACKWARDATION, the first since 10-August. SPREAD AND FLAT PRICE MOVED IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS. All week the pattern was the reverse - new highs on a loosening front end - and read together the two configurations say the same thing from opposite ends: the marginal price-setter is positioned in the forward tenors, not at the prompt date. Keep it in proportion. $4.00 is 0.12% of cash: a marginal prompt premium, not a squeeze, and the front end has not held a premium two sessions running since 04-August.

THE PROXIMATE CAUSE OF THE TWO-SESSION DECLINE, AND IT IS A GENUINE CHANGE IN THE 2027 SUPPLY PICTURE. Emirates Global Aluminium's H1-2026 earnings release, published 12-August, disclosed that the Al Taweelah smelter in Abu Dhabi - shut by a missile strike in March and restarted in May - is currently running at about 18% of capacity, and guided hot metal production back to pre-incident levels in Q1-2027, with roughly US$400 million of capital allocated to the recovery programme. At the time of the May restart the company had expected a return to full capacity to take about a year. THE MARKET READ THIS AS AN ACCELERATION AND SOLD IT: prices snapped a seven-session rally on 12-August and extended the fall on 13-August. The region accounted for around a tenth of global primary production before the conflict. NOTE WHAT THIS IS AND IS NOT: it is a dated path back to normal for the single largest damaged asset in the market. It is not a tonne of metal available next week, which is why the forward tenors sold harder than the prompt date and the curve flipped into backwardation on the same session.

THE SECOND SUPPLY-RELIEF HEADLINE IN TWO DAYS AND THE ONE WITH THE LONGEST TAIL. Tomago Aluminium - Australia's largest smelter at up to 590,000 t/y, almost 40% of Australian production, and New South Wales' largest single electricity user - secured a A$2.5 billion federal and state support package on 13-August. It will enter a ten-year power purchase agreement after its existing contract expires on 31-December-2028, taking electricity supply to 2038 and to fully renewable sources from 2033, and will invest A$1.1 billion in real terms through 2038 including A$100 million for decarbonisation. The shift to renewables is expected to cut Scope 1 and 2 operating emissions by 7.1 Mt/y from 2033. The smelter will continue providing demand-response services during grid stress. Ownership is Rio Tinto 51.55%, Gove Aluminium Finance 36.05% and Norsk Hydro 12.4%. The deal follows a March agreement securing the Boyne smelter in Gladstone. A CLOSURE RISK OVER ROUGHLY HALF A MILLION TONNES A YEAR HAS BEEN REMOVED, and the pattern - a smelter of that scale needing public support to contract power at all - is itself the most honest available public statement about western smelter economics.

MARGINS EXPANDED SHARPLY DESPITE A THIRD OF THE VOLUME GONE - THE CLEANEST READ ON GULF SMELTER ECONOMICS AVAILABLE THIS CYCLE. EGA reported H1-2026 adjusted net profit of Dh2.46 billion, up 34% year-on-year, and adjusted EBITDA of Dh4.51 billion, up 11%, with the adjusted EBITDA margin widening to 33.3% from 27.0%. Revenue FELL 10% to Dh13.54 billion because aluminium sales dropped 32% to 939,000 tonnes and cast metal production fell 29% to 1.01 million tonnes. Reported net income was Dh1.74 billion after a Dh725 million net impact from the March incident, and the company estimates around Dh1.5 billion of capital expenditure to restore Al Taweelah with most of it falling in 2026. THE COMPOSITION IS THE POINT: profit rose on higher realised prices, stronger regional premiums and LOWER ALUMINA PRICES while a third of the volume was unavailable. That is a direct, publicly disclosed confirmation of the margin structure this board has been describing all cycle - a cheap alumina leg carrying smelter profitability.

THIRD DAY AT HALF RATE, NO RESTART DATE, AND STILL NO PRICE PRINT TO SIZE IT. Norsk Hydro's Alunorte refinery in Barcarena - 6.3 Mt/y nameplate and the largest alumina refinery outside China - remains at 50% of capacity after gas supplier CELBA notified disruptions to natural gas availability. The company guides a potential Q3-2026 Bauxite & Alumina impact of US$75-100 million while calling the full impact uncertain, and says it will ramp back 'as soon as gas availability normalizes'. Roughly 3 Mt/y of annualised seaborne alumina is off the balance. THE ABSENCE OF A PRICE PRINT IS ITSELF THE STORY AT THIS POINT: three days on, no public seaborne alumina transaction dated after the disclosure has appeared, which means the market has not yet had to clear a cargo into the new reality. The first print that does is the datapoint that converts this headline into a cost fact. The supplier issue is gas AVAILABILITY rather than price, which is harder to solve quickly than a commercial dispute.

A 32ND CONSECUTIVE DRAW TOOK STOCK TO A FRESH CYCLE LOW ON THE SECOND DOWN DAY RUNNING. LME aluminium inventory fell another 1,700 t to 250,000 t. Six weeks of uninterrupted daily draws is the single strongest public argument for physical tightness on this board, and it has now continued through a two-session, $94.00 decline - which is precisely when a financially-motivated draw would be expected to pause. Today it was joined by a supporting signal rather than a contradicting one: the cash-3M spread flipped into backwardation on the same session. Copper told an identical story - stock down 4,400 t to 207,725 t while its backwardation widened from $175.00 to $203.00.

CHINESE BUYERS STOOD ASIDE INTO THE WEEKEND, AND THE SELLERS BLINKED FIRST. SMM's 14-August South China spot review reports futures extending sharp losses with spot 'in the doldrums'. Holders initially tried to sell at firm prices in the morning but, as bearish sentiment built ahead of the weekend and the willingness to cash out early increased, most lowered prices to offer discounts; mainstream quotations sat at discounts of -10 to 0 yuan/mt with supply relatively ample. Downstream buyers initially stayed on the sidelines expecting lower prices, then restocked at the lows in limited volume, and traders mainly pushed for lower prices to absorb discounted cargoes. Transactions concentrated at premiums of 60-100 yuan/mt over the SHFE 2608 contract. THE ONE CONSTRUCTIVE DETAIL IN THE SAME REPORT, AND IT SHOULD NOT BE BURIED: inventory has returned to a destocking path.

THE DOWNSTREAM COST CHAIN IS FOLLOWING THE METAL DOWN. SMM reports ADC12 secondary alloy quotes generally lowered a further 200 yuan/mt on 14-August. The reduction is attributed to the pullback in aluminium prices, the subsequent decline in aluminium scrap prices that pushed costs lower, and a weaker cast aluminium alloy futures market leaving cost-side support somewhat weakened. Secondary alloy is the marginal substitute for primary metal in a range of casting applications, so a falling ADC12 quote is simultaneously a symptom of weaker primary demand and a mild additional drag on it.

INDIA PASSED A NEW MINING BILL ON 13-AUGUST, intended to improve flexibility, revenue and tax certainty for mining companies. It takes effect once it receives presidential assent. India is the fastest-growing significant non-Chinese primary aluminium producer and a substantial bauxite jurisdiction, and its integrated producers have just reported record upstream quarters, so the regime governing its mining sector is a genuine structural input to the non-Chinese supply picture. It is tagged Mixed rather than directional because the practical effect - more investment certainty, therefore more supply, but on a multi-year horizon - cuts both ways for price and is years from a tonne.

backtest.verdict: These condition indicators showed NO predictive edge when tested: a 38.4% directional hit rate against a 71.2% naive 'always higher' baseline over the same sample, and forward returns after 'tightening' readings averaged 1.75% versus 7.04% after 'loosening' readings. They are therefore published as a read on CURRENT market condition only — not as a price forecast. The forward baseline and probability range above are the forward-looking view.

THIS IS THE CLEANEST PUBLIC EVIDENCE AVAILABLE OF HOW AN INTEGRATED PRODUCER CONVERTS THE 2026 PRICE STRUCTURE INTO MARGIN, AND THE CONVERSION RATE IS VERY HIGH. Revenue rose 32% while EBITDA rose 73% and upstream aluminium EBITDA rose 81% - operating leverage of well over two times on the upstream leg. The mechanism is integration: captive bauxite, captive alumina and captive coal-fired power insulate the cost stack from exactly the two legs that are currently rising for non-integrated smelters, namely seaborne bauxite (SMM index $71.57/mt, +$0.70 w/w) and seaborne alumina ($356/mt FOB East Australia on the 05-Aug trade). catalysts.text: THE 14-AUGUST LME OFFICIAL, AND SPECIFICALLY WHETHER THE $4.00 BACKWARDATION SURVIVES A THIRD SESSION. This is the highest-information event on the calendar and the test is precise. A PROMPT PREMIUM THAT PERSISTS OR WIDENS WHILE FLAT PRICE FALLS AGAIN would be the first genuine evidence in this cycle that the physical market is tightening independently of financial positioning, and it would argue the two-day sell-off is a repricing of 2027 rather than of the prompt balance. A SLIP BACK INTO CONTANGO marks today's flip as noise and returns the read to the one that has held since 04-August - a front end that will not hold a premium two days running. A THIRD DECLINE WITH A WIDENING CONTANGO would be the bearish outcome and would put the 05-August wave (iv) low at $3,229.50 directly in play. Watch the stock line alongside: a 33rd consecutive draw on a third down day would sharpen the divergence further, and any interruption to it removes the bull case's best evidence.

MONTHLY CARBON SETTLEMENT WINDOW - prebaked anodes, coal tar pitch and green petroleum coke settle around the 17th-18th. This is the next scheduled opportunity to append sourced marks to the input-basket histories for those rows, all of which are currently carried at their June or July cycles. The risk into the window is modestly to the upside for smelter carbon: Brent has spent August well above the pre-crisis reference and green coke is a refinery by-product, so crude strength feeds the calcining chain with a lag - though Brent has now softened for two sessions on the Hormuz stalemate, which cuts the other way with an even longer lag.

MJP Q4-2026 PREMIUM NEGOTIATIONS conventionally open against the Q3-2026 settlement of $395/t CIF Japan. Nothing dated after the 06-July settlement has published. THE ARGUMENTS ON BOTH SIDES STRENGTHENED THIS WEEK, WHICH IS WHY THE SCENARIO RANGE IS HELD. Sellers will point at 32 consecutive stock draws to a fresh cycle low, a front end that flipped back into backwardation, and Alunorte at 50%. Buyers now have something they did not have a week ago: two dated public supply-relief facts in EGA's Q1-2027 recovery path and the Tomago power settlement to 2038, plus the CIF Japan spot reference sitting $25/t BELOW the settled quarterly number and a yen at 159.45 that raises the local-currency cost of any dollar premium. Three days have passed without a follow-up disclosure. The two things to watch are a further Section 5-12 disclosure from the company and the first public seaborne alumina transaction print dated after 11-August. THE SECOND IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS MOST TO THIS BOARD: it is what converts a supply headline into a cost fact, and until it arrives the entire cost consequence of a 3 Mt/y annualised outage is unpriced here. Note the asymmetry it would create with the peer-earnings panel - EGA's H1 margin expansion was explicitly attributed in part to LOWER alumina prices, so an alumina repricing compresses the Gulf fleet's margin first.

risks.text: SUPPLY RELIEF ARRIVES ON A DATED, PUBLISHED SCHEDULE AND CAPS THE RECOVERY - THE RISK THAT MATERIALISED THIS WEEK AND THE REASON THE PRICE FELL. For months the returning capacity on this board was a list of intentions. In 48 hours two of them acquired dates and numbers: EGA's H1 release on 12-August put Al Taweelah at about 18% of capacity with pre-incident hot metal guided for Q1-2027 and roughly US$400m allocated; and on 13-August Tomago, up to 590,000 t/y, was secured by a A$2.5bn support package with power contracted to 2038. Add Slovalco's 75,000 t/y in Q4-2026, Magnitude 7 Metals' 75,000 t/y at New Madrid before year-end, Mt. Holly already at full capacity, and SMM's outside-China daily average output already +1.6% month-on-month in July. TREND UP, AND RAISED TO HIGH IMPACT: this is no longer a forecast, it is a published schedule, and the market took $94.00 out of the price in two sessions on the first two entries in it.

ALUNORTE GAS DISRUPTION EXTENDS AND BECOMES AN ALUMINA COST SHOCK. Day three at 50 percent with no restart date, no follow-up disclosure, and a company-guided potential Q3-2026 impact of US$75-100 million. Roughly 3 Mt/y of annualised seaborne alumina is out. The supplier issue is gas AVAILABILITY rather than price, which is harder to solve quickly than a commercial dispute, and the contingency measures announced - spot gas purchases and a request for direct LNG terminal access - are themselves evidence that the contracted route is not working. TREND UP: a third day without resolution makes an extended outage more likely than it was at disclosure, and three days on no public alumina price print has arrived to size the market impact - which means the cost consequence is still entirely unpriced on this board.

PROLONGED HORMUZ CLOSURE KEEPS GULF SUPPLY IMPAIRED - AND THE MARKET HAS JUST DEMONSTRATED HOW SENSITIVE IT IS TO ANY CHANGE IN THAT ASSUMPTION. Day 166 since the 28-February shutdown, with no development reported since Iran's state broadcaster restated on 11-August that the Strait remains closed until conditions are met; Trading Economics' 14-August stream frames both crude benchmarks as holding declines 'amid Hormuz stalemate'. The Gulf was around a tenth of global primary production pre-conflict. TREND FLAT: nothing changed in substance this run. But note the calibration today provided free of charge - repricing ONE Gulf smelter's recovery date moved the market nearly 3% in two sessions, so a change in the Strait regime itself would be an order of magnitude larger, in either direction.

POSITIONING UNWIND IN A CROWDED LONG. This desk argued for a week that a rally making new highs while the front end surrendered its premium was carried by expectation rather than prompt need. $94.00 has now come out of the price in two sessions. TREND DOWN, AND FOR A SECOND REASON TODAY BEYOND THE SIMPLE FACT THAT SOME OF IT HAS DISCHARGED: the front end flipped INTO a $4.00 backwardation on the second down day, which is the opposite of what a continuing liquidation would produce. Length leaving a market normally loosens the prompt date; today it tightened. The residual exposure is materially lower than it was at $3,374.00.

THE STOCK DRAW STOPS OR REVERSES AND REMOVES THE BULL CASE'S BEST EVIDENCE. Six weeks of consecutive draws are the single strongest public argument for tightness, and the argument dies the day metal starts returning to warrant. TREND DOWN: today provided evidence AGAINST this risk for a second consecutive session - the draw continued for a 32nd session to a fresh cycle low of 250,000 t, and it did so on a second down day, which is precisely when a financially-motivated draw would be expected to pause. Copper drew 4,400 t on the same session. The one honest caveat: 250,000 t is a round number and round numbers attract attention.

CHINESE PHYSICAL DEMAND WEAKENS AT THIS PRICE LEVEL. SMM's 14-August South China review has holders lowering offers into discounts of -10 to 0 yuan/mt as bearish sentiment built into the weekend, downstream buyers standing aside on expectations of lower prices, and traders pushing for discounted cargoes; ADC12 secondary alloy quotes were cut a further 200 yuan/mt on falling metal and scrap costs. China is roughly 60% of global output and the marginal consumer of most seaborne units. TREND UP: buyer resistance has now been reported explicitly for three consecutive sessions and is being reported on the way DOWN as well as at the top, which is the more concerning version - it says the resistance is to the level, not just to the rate of change. The one offset in the same report: inventory has returned to a destocking path.

MACRO TIGHTENING RAISES THE COST OF CARRYING COMMODITY LENGTH. Industrial metals are positioning-sensitive and long-dated financing costs bite hardest when a rally is carried by financial rather than consumer demand. TREND DOWN: the macro backdrop was benign again this run and was NOT the constraint. The dollar index was essentially flat at 99.904, the US 10-year eased to 4.649% and the euro was marginally firmer. Note the awkward implication for the bull case, stated honestly: aluminium fell for a second session anyway, which points the explanation firmly at the two supply headlines rather than at financial conditions.

Rio Tinto's 40% Yarwun alumina cut from October 2026 trims one input to that surplus REVIEWED 13-AUG: no balance-relevant datapoint changed on 12-August. Exchange inventory drew for a 31st consecutive session, 1,700 t to 251,700 t, and the draw rate ACCELERATED from the 1,500 t/day that had run for six of the seven prior sessions - the tightening in visible metal continued on a day the price fell 1.94%. Against that, Alunorte remains at 50 percent with roughly 3 Mt/y of seaborne alumina out, which is an upstream cost event rather than a metal balance event and should not be double-counted as a supply deficit for primary aluminium.
